metrics.label: share of injected degradations the detector opened an incident for
metrics.note: one trial out of the eighteen the gate profile runs. The spread across 8 seeds was exactly zero — the same three trials miss every time — so a band from the standard deviation would be zero and would fire the first time any scenario went the other way. One trial is the quantum of a rate measured over eighteen of them.

metrics.note: hand-set, not derived. All eight seeds returned zero at gate size, so the spread offers no band at all — and zero is the wrong claim: the full profile returns three, because over forty-five minutes an incident ramps, peaks and recovers, and the lever that suits a rail at 20% is not the one that suits it at 45%. Three changes is evolution; more than three in a twenty-minute window is flapping, which is the failure mode worth catching.

metrics.note: widened from ₹5,000 when the population became multilingual. The old band was 3 sd of a monolingual world; opt-outs are a small integer count and a baseline that half its readers cannot read produces more of them, so the seed-to-seed coefficient of variation on this metric went from 17.4% to 33.7%. ₹10,000 is about 3 sd of the new spread. A band this wide catches breakage rather than degradation and is listed as such in the gate's own note.

metrics.label: messages sent — the term the contact cap and the opt-out cost are both about
share of the baseline's messages that reached somebody in a script they read — the size of the problem the copy library exists to solve, measured on the arm that does not solve it
metrics.note: 3 sd over 8 seeds, rounded up. The steadiest metric on the recovery scorecard (cv 1.67%) because it is a property of the population rather than of any decision: it is roughly the English share of customers, and drifts only as the sample does. It is gated because a change here means either the language mix or the template arm's copy moved, and both should be deliberate.

metrics.label: what generated copy recovered over the same system running templates, at the default readability penalty — a figure that goes to zero if that penalty is wrong
metrics.note: ₹1,00,000 against a mean of ₹78,509 — a band wider than the value it guards, and deliberately so. The seed-to-seed coefficient of variation is 37.6%, the highest on the scorecard, because this is a difference between two noisy quantities and differences of noisy quantities are noisier than either. The honest reading is that the gain is positive and its magnitude is not resolvable at this sample size; the gate can therefore only catch it disappearing, which is what it is for. Do not quote this metric's point value as a finding — quote the multi-seed legibility sweep in the recovery report.
